proved.statement: For arbitrary symmetric S and independent cap-one physical coordinates, if two original-coordinate rows into a disjoint bank have Gram determinant D>0, then |phi_R(t)|<=min(1,pi*sqrt(2)*D^(-1/4)/|t|), int|phi_R|^(3/2)<=6*pi*sqrt(2)*D^(-1/4), and ||p_R||_3<=3^(2/3)*2^(1/3)*D^(-1/6). Arbitrary self terms, mutual edge, bank quadratic phase, and all outside couplings are retained.
proved.regularity: absolute continuity with L3 density; continuity not asserted

proved.statement: After completing one nonzero physical scalar pivot a, if the Schur residual has such a pair-wedge D>0, then ||p_Q||_infinity <= 2^(15/4)*3^(-1/4)*|a|^(-1/2)*D^(-1/8) = 10.223089667940359... |a|^(-1/2)D^(-1/8).
proved.regularity: essentially bounded density; continuity not proved

proved.statement: For natural squared-3-volume law of a physical cross block M with Z=e3(M^TM), pair inclusion mass p_ik satisfies p_ik Z = D_ik R_ik, where D_ik=||r_i wedge r_k||^2 and R_ik is total squared energy of all other rows after projection orthogonal to span(r_i,r_k). If alpha_i>1/2 and P(k|i)>1/2 then D_ik R_ik>Z/4.

partner_application.partner_fact: For heavy row h, e2(N^TN)>=alpha Z/||r_h||^2 after deleting h.
partner_application.new_inequality: If one residual physical pair carries fraction theta of this e2, then ||p_Q||_infinity <= C_* |a|^(-1/2)[theta alpha Z/||r_h||^2]^(-1/8), C_*=10.223089667940359...

preserved_corrections: No law-uniform positive-power pointwise decay for one arbitrary-density quadratic phase; phase-aligned fragmented supports remain a counterexample.
Do not infer a uniformly good physical pair/minor from the three-large-eigenvalue hypothesis.

first_unpaid_implication.statement: When clustered natural 3-volume leaves the partner-guaranteed e2 spread over many physical row pairs, spend the whole pair-volume jointly, using variable-order/fractional Brascamp-Lieb or a grouped transverse-bank recursion, before selecting a physical pair. Preserve p_ik Z=D_ik R_ik as normalization.

checker.role: sanity/regression only; analytic proof is canonical
